subsystems.name: Cryo-CMOS control ASIC
subsystems.role: generates qubit control pulses and reads return signals from inside the refrigerator instead of from a rack at room temperature.

subsystems.name: Multiplexing network
subsystems.role: lets one cable serve many qubits, which is the whole point of the exercise.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic interconnect
subsystems.role: carries signals and heat between the refrigerator's temperature stages.
parts: low-loss coaxial and flexible ribbon cables

subsystems.name: Thermal budget
subsystems.role: keeps the added electronics inside the very small cooling power available at each stage.

subsystems.name: Room-temperature interface
subsystems.role: the only remaining wide link to the outside world.

subsystems.name: Calibration software
subsystems.role: maps desired quantum operations onto the reduced pulse set the cryo chip can produce.

buildSteps.title: Choose the process
buildSteps.detail: A mature CMOS node is picked for low leakage and reliable behaviour when cooled, rather than for maximum speed.

buildSteps.title: Measure transistors cold
buildSteps.detail: Devices are characterised at liquid-helium and millikelvin temperatures, because foundry models only describe room-temperature behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Design the ASIC
buildSteps.detail: Converters, mixers and control logic are laid out so that the chip's own power dissipation — perhaps a few milliwatts — fits the refrigerator's budget.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and package
buildSteps.detail: The chip is made at a commercial foundry, thinned, and mounted on a package that survives repeated thermal cycling.

buildSteps.title: Characterise in a dilution refrigerator
buildSteps.detail: The packaged chip is cooled and tested for noise, timing jitter and crosstalk at its operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Wire into the fridge
buildSteps.detail: Cables, filters and attenuators are threaded through the stages with thermal anchoring so heat does not reach the coldest plate.

buildSteps.title: Validate with real qubits
buildSteps.detail: The chip drives superconducting qubits and its gate fidelities are compared against conventional room-temperature electronics.

buildSteps.title: Scale the tile
buildSteps.detail: Several identical chips are daisy-chained on one refrigeration stage so that hundreds of qubits share a small number of cables.

prerequisites.tech: Dilution refrigerators with known heat budgets
prerequisites.why: cooling power at the coldest stage is well under a milliwatt, so every milliwatt of control electronics must be placed higher up or removed.
cryo control only matters once qubit counts outgrow the number of coaxial lines a fridge can carry.

prerequisites.tech: Cryogenic transistor models and design kits
prerequisites.why: without accurate cold models, chips must be designed conservatively and re-spun after measurement.
sharing lines between qubits depends on frequency-multiplexed readout that preserves fidelity.
the chips ride on ordinary silicon manufacturing, which keeps them cheap once designed.

pathway.milestone: cryo-CMOS chips running a handful of qubits from the few-kelvin stage (chipmakers such as Intel have demonstrated this with Horse Ridge)
pathway.unlocks: proof that control electronics can survive and work inside the fridge.

pathway.milestone: multiplexed control of tens to low hundreds of qubits per chip, with cold device models shared by foundries
pathway.unlocks: fridges that host arrays big enough for early error correction.

pathway.milestone: control functions pushed to the millikelvin stage and combined with cryogenic readout amplifiers
pathway.unlocks: a single cable or optical fibre carrying the whole control and readout load.

pathway.milestone: wafer-scale or chiplet cryo controllers matched to thousands of physical qubits per refrigerator
pathway.unlocks: fault-tolerant quantum computers that are not limited by wiring.
